items.title: B.C. Patient Care Quality Review
items.description: The Ministry of Health is reviewing B.C.'s patient-care-quality system, including how it responds to Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination.
items.why_watching: The review may lead to policy direction and legislative change, and it overlaps with accountability concerns raised in In Plain Sight.
items.next_question: What policy or legislative recommendations will the review publish, and how will Indigenous participation shape them?

items.title: Island Health Indigenous Patient Self-Identification redesign
items.description: Island Health paused its Indigenous Patient Self-Identification Program after feedback from First Nations leaders and communities, and committed to a distinctions-based redesign with First Nations and Métis partners.
items.why_watching: The next public evidence should clarify data-governance commitments, decision authority and conditions for resuming the program.
items.next_question: What redesign milestones, governance agreements and resumption conditions will Island Health publish?

items.title: B.C. health anti-racism and cultural-safety centre
items.description: B.C.'s 2026–28 Anti-Racism Action Plan commits to a new Ministry of Health centre focused on anti-racism and cultural safety.
items.why_watching: Creation, mandate and public reporting will show how a government commitment becomes an operating accountability mechanism.
items.next_question: When will the centre begin operating, what authority will it have and how will Indigenous governance be represented?

sources.title: B.C. releases Anti-Racism Action Plan for 2026–28

items.title: Public response to FNHO recommendations
items.description: Saskatchewan's Health Minister stated that the Ministry and Saskatchewan Health Authority were reviewing the First Nations Health Ombudsperson Office's inaugural report and recommendations.
items.why_watching: A later comprehensive public response or recommendation-by-recommendation implementation account was not located in the bounded sources reviewed.
items.next_question: Will the Ministry or health authority publish a formal response, action plan or progress account?

sources.title: First Nations Health Ombudsperson Office annual report
Saskatchewan Legislative Assembly Debates and Proceedings

items.title: Anti-Indigenous Racism Navigator Network
items.description: Federal UN Declaration Act reporting describes a Saskatchewan network for navigators from First Nations organizations to collaborate and exchange resources.
items.why_watching: The public description establishes the network's purpose, but not a participant list, governance terms, outcomes or a public reporting cycle.
items.next_question: Which organizations participate, how is the network governed and what implementation evidence will be reported?

sources.title: UN Declaration Act Action Plan progress reporting

items.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate
items.description: Alberta's Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate receives concerns, conducts delegated reviews under the Health Charter and provides advice and recommendations.
items.why_watching: Public activity and follow-up reporting can show how this accountability mechanism operates in practice while preserving its stated remit and limits.
items.next_question: What aggregate activity, recommendations and health-system responses will be publicly reported?

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate

items.title: Indigenous Cultural Safety evidence review
items.description: Alberta lists a completed 2025 evidence review of interventions intended to reduce racism toward Indigenous peoples in healthcare.
items.why_watching: The review may provide an evidence base for later policy and implementation choices, but its relationship to particular program decisions needs source-backed follow-up.
items.next_question: Which current Alberta programs or policies explicitly rely on the review's findings?

items.title: Alberta Indigenous health anti-racism strategy
items.description: Alberta held 38 engagement sessions in 2024 and stated that a What We Heard report and Indigenous health anti-racism strategy would follow.
items.why_watching: A final report or strategy was not located on the program page or in the bounded official-source search, so the next public milestone remains unclear.
items.next_question: Will Alberta publish the engagement report, final strategy and an implementation timetable?

sources.title: Addressing racism in Indigenous health care
